In standard geological and mining operations, the definitive verified conclusion establishes that: F = C + 2 - P (or P <= C) (At arbitrary pressure and temperature where variance F >= 2, the number of coexisting phases does not exceed components: P <= C; Gibbs rule is F = C + 2 - P).

Fails to meet the specific technical requirements of the problem statement.

(C) Orthoclase
(D) Albite
Part I

Applied Geology & Mining Engineering Foundations

1. Applied Geology & Mining Engineering Foundations

This problem evaluates Feldspar Mineralogy: High-Temperature Disordered Sanidine within the framework of Mineralogy & Crystallography.

In standard geological and mining operations, the definitive verified conclusion establishes that: Sanidine (Sanidine is the high-temperature, monoclinic disordered form of K-feldspar (KAlSi3O8) stable above ~500°C in rapidly quenched felsic volcanic rocks).

Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, 3rd Ed., Ch. 13, pp. 310-325); Cornelis Klein (Manual of Mineral Science, Ch. 19)

Part II

Option (A): Sanidine — CORRECT ANSWER

Accurately satisfies the foundational geological definition and official examination standard.

Option (B): Microcline . — INCORRECT

Represents an alternative or non-applicable parameter.

Option (C): Orthoclase — INCORRECT

Fails to meet the specific technical requirements of the problem statement.

Option (D): Albite — INCORRECT

Incompatible with the established engineering geology and resource evaluation criteria.

Part I

Applied Geology & Mining Engineering Foundations

This problem evaluates Volcanology: Pyroclastic Density Current Deposits within the framework of Igneous & Metamorphic Petrology.

In standard geological and mining operations, the definitive verified conclusion establishes that: Ignimbrite (Ignimbrite is a poorly sorted pyroclastic rock formed by the consolidation and welding of pumice and ash from explosive pyroclastic density currents).

Part I

Applied Geology & Mining Engineering Foundations

1. Applied Geology & Mining Engineering Foundations

This problem evaluates Plate Tectonics: Convergent Destructive Margins within the framework of Structural Geology & Tectonics.

In standard geological and mining operations, the definitive verified conclusion establishes that: Converging plate boundary (Convergent margins (subduction zones) are termed destructive plate boundaries because oceanic lithosphere is consumed back into the mantle).

Kearey, Klepeis & Vine (Global Tectonics, 3rd Ed., Ch. 5 & 7, pp. 110-140); Lowrie (Ch. 1)

Option (C): Converging plate boundary — CORRECT ANSWER

Incompatible with the established engineering geology and resource evaluation criteria.
